source_text:
Gnosticus (fragmenta Graeca)
Ο ΓΝΩΣΤΙΚΟΣ Η ΠΡΟΣ ΤΟΝ ΚΑΤΑΞΙΩΘΕΝΤΑ ΓΝΩΣΕΩΣ
1 Πρακτικοὶ λόγους νοήσουσι πρακτικούς, γνωστικοὶ δὲ ὄψονται γνωστικά.
2 Πρακτικὸς μέν ἐστιν ὁ τὸ παθητικὸν μέρος τῆς ψυχῆς μόνον ἀπαθὲς
κεκτημένος.
3 Γνωστικὸς δὲ ὁ ἁλὸς μὲν λόγον ἐπέχων τοῖς ἀκαθάρτοις, φωτὸς δὲ τοῖς
καθαροῖς.
4 Ἡ μὲν ἔξωθεν ἡμῖν συμβαίνουσα γνῶσις, διὰ τῶν λόγων ὑποδεικνύειν
πειρᾶται τὰς ὕλας· ἡ δὲ ἐκ Θεοῦ χάριτος ἐγγινομένη, αὐτοψεὶ τῇ διανοίᾳ παρίστησι
τὰ πράγματα, πρὸς ἃ βλέπων ὁ νοῦς, τοὺς αὐτῶν λόγους προσίεται· ἀντίκειται δὲ τῇ
μὲν προτέρᾳ ἡ πλάνη· τῇ δὲ δευτέρᾳ ὀργὴ καὶ θυμός· καὶ τὰ τούτοις
παρακολουθοῦντα.
5 Πᾶσαι τῷ γνωστικῷ ὁδοποιοῦσιν αἱ ἀρεταί· ὑπὲρ δὲ πάσας ἡ ἀοργησία. Ὁ
γὰρ γνώσεως ἐφαψάμενος καὶ πρὸς ὀργὴν ῥᾳδίως κινούμενος, ὅμοιός ἐστι τῷ σιδηρᾷ
περόνῃ τοὺς ἑαυτοῦ ὀφθαλμοὺς κατανύττοντι.
6 Ἀσφαλιζέσθω δὲ ἐν ταῖς συγκαταβάσεσιν ὁ γνωστικός, μήποτε λάθῃ αὐτὸν
ἕξις γινομένη ἡ συγκατάβασις, καὶ πειράσθω πάσας ἐπίσης ἀεὶ τὰς ἀρετὰς
κατορθοῦν, ἵνα ἀντακολουθῶσιν ἀλλήλαις καὶ ἐν αὐτῷ, διὰ τὸ πεφυκέναι τὸν νοῦν
ὑπὸ τῆς ἐλαττουμένης προδίδοσθαι.
8 Αἰσχρὸν γνωστικῷ τὸ δικάζεσθαι καὶ ἀδικουμένῳ καὶ ἀδικοῦντι·
ἀδικουμένῳ μὲν ὅτι οὐχ ὑπέμεινεν, ἀδικοῦντι δὲ ὅτι ἠδίκησε.
9 Ἡ γνῶσις συντηρουμένη διδάσκει τὸν μετέχοντα αὐτῆς ὅπως ἂν
διαφυλαχθῇ καὶ ἐπὶ μείζονα προέλθοι.
13 ∆ίκαιον τοῖς μοναχοῖς καὶ τοῖς κοσμικοῖς περὶ πολιτείας ὀρθῆς
διαλέγεσθαι καὶ ὅσα τῆς φυσικῆς ἢ θεολογικῆς δόγματα σαφηνίζειν ἐκ μέρους, ὧν
χωρὶς οὐδεὶς ὄψεται τὸν Κύριον. 15 Γνώριζε καιρῶν καὶ βίων καὶ ἐπιτηδευμάτων
τοὺς λόγους καὶ τοὺς νόμους, ἵνα ἔχῃς ἑκάστῳ τὰ συμφέροντα ῥᾳδίως λέγειν.
orientation: Evagrius opens the treatise by defining the practical ascetic and the gnostic, then gives counsels on the virtues, especially freedom from anger, and on the gnostic's speech and conduct.
pass_a_gloss: Practical ascetics will understand practical words, but gnostics will see gnostic things. The practical ascetic is the one who has acquired only the passionate part of the soul as free from passion. The gnostic is the one who holds the place of salt for the impure, but of light for the pure. The knowledge that comes to us from outside tries to point out the materials through words; but the knowledge that comes to be in us from the grace of God presents the things themselves to the mind by direct vision, looking at which the mind receives their principles; and error is opposed to the former, but anger and wrath and the things that follow these are opposed to the latter. All the virtues make a road for the gnostic; but above all, freedom from anger. For the one who has touched knowledge and is easily moved to anger is like the one who pierces his own eyes with an iron pin. Let the gnostic be on guard in his accommodations, lest the accommodation become a fixed habit without his noticing, and let him try always to accomplish all the virtues equally, so that they follow one another also in him, because the mind is naturally betrayed by the virtue that is lacking. It is shameful for a gnostic to go to court, both when he is wronged and when he does wrong; when he is wronged, because he did not endure; when he does wrong, because he did wrong. Knowledge, when it is preserved, teaches the one who partakes of it how he may be kept safe and advance to greater things. It is right for monks and for people in the world to discuss correct conduct and to clarify in part the doctrines of natural and theological knowledge, without which no one will see the Lord. Know the principles and laws of times and lives and occupations, so that you may easily say what is beneficial to each person.

choices.term: ὁ ἁλὸς μὲν λόγον ἐπέχων τοῖς ἀκαθάρτοις, φωτὸς δὲ τοῖς καθαροῖς
choices.english: the one who holds the place of salt for the impure, but of light for the pure
choices.why: Keeps the metaphor of salt and light as roles the gnostic fills, preserving the contrast between impure and pure.
rejected: the one who is salt to the impure and light to the pure
the one who serves as salt for the impure and light for the pure

choices.term: αὐτοψεὶ τῇ διανοίᾳ παρίστησι τὰ πράγματα
choices.english: presents the things themselves to the mind by direct vision
choices.why: Renders the adverb 'autopsei' as 'by direct vision' to convey immediate, unmediated presentation, distinct from the external knowledge that works through words.
rejected: shows the things to the mind face to face
presents the realities to the mind with its own eyes

choices.term: ἀντίκειται δὲ τῇ μὲν προτέρᾳ ἡ πλάνη· τῇ δὲ δευτέρᾳ ὀργὴ καὶ θυμός
choices.english: and error is opposed to the former, but anger and wrath and the things that follow these are opposed to the latter
choices.why: Preserves the parallel structure of opposition to the two kinds of knowledge, keeping 'error' for the external knowledge and 'anger and wrath' for the grace-given knowledge.
rejected: error opposes the first, anger and wrath oppose the second
the first is opposed by error, the second by anger and wrath

choices.why: Keeps the verbal force of 'hodopoieo' as making a path or road, conveying that the virtues prepare the way for the gnostic.

choices.english: Let the gnostic be on guard in his accommodations
choices.why: Renders the middle imperative 'asphalizestho' as 'be on guard' and keeps 'accommodations' for the glossary term 'sygkatabasis', preserving the warning tone.
rejected: Let the gnostic secure himself in his condescensions
Let the gnostic take care in his stooping down

choices.english: is betrayed by the virtue that is lacking
choices.why: Keeps the passive 'prodidosthai' as 'is betrayed' and renders 'elattoumenes' as 'that is lacking' to convey that the mind is undone by whichever virtue is deficient.
rejected: is given away by the lesser virtue
is handed over by the diminished virtue

bible_refs.note: The gnostic as salt for the impure and light for the pure echoes the sayings about salt and light.
The phrase 'without which no one will see the Lord' echoes the call to holiness without which no one will see the Lord.

pass_b_english: Practical ascetics will understand practical words, and gnostics will see gnostic things.
A practical ascetic is one who has acquired only the passionate part of the soul as free from passion.
A gnostic is one who serves as salt for the impure, and as light for the pure.

The knowledge that comes to us from outside tries to point out material things through words, but the knowledge that arises within by God's grace presents the things themselves to the mind by direct vision. The mind looks at these things and receives their principles. Error is opposed to the former kind of knowledge, but anger and wrath and the things that follow these are opposed to the latter.

All the virtues make a road for the gnostic, but above all, freedom from anger. For the one who has grasped spiritual knowledge and is easily moved to anger is like a man piercing his own eyes with an iron pin.

Let the gnostic be on guard in his accommodations, lest accommodation secretly become a fixed habit in him. And let him strive always to practice all the virtues equally, so that they follow one another in him, because the mind is naturally betrayed by the virtue that is lacking.
It is shameful for a gnostic to go to court, whether he has been wronged or has wronged another: if he has been wronged, because he did not endure it; if he has wronged another, because he did wrong.
Spiritual knowledge, when it is guarded, teaches the one who shares in it how he may be preserved and advance to greater things.
It is right to discuss correct conduct with monks and people in the world and to clarify in part the teachings of natural and theological doctrine, without which no one will see the Lord.
Learn the principles and laws of times, ways of life, and occupations, so that you may readily say what is beneficial to each person.

problems.quote: A practical ascetic is one who has acquired only the passionate part of the soul as free from passion.
problems.source_quote: Πρακτικὸς μὲν ἐστιν ὁ τὸ παθητικὸν μέρος τῆς ψυχῆς μόνον ἀπαθὲς κεκτημένος.
problems.why: The Greek says “the passive part of the soul,” not “the passionate part.”
problems.fix: A practical ascetic is one who has acquired only the passive part of the soul, which is free from passion.

problems.quote: It is right to discuss correct conduct with monks and with people in the world, and to clarify in part the teachings of natural and theological doctrine, without which no one will see the Lord (Hebrews 12:14).
problems.source_quote: Δίκαιον τοῖς μοναχοῖς καὶ τοῖς κοσμικοῖς περὶ πολιτείας ὀρθῆς διαλέγεσθαι καὶ ὅσα τῆς φυσικῆς ἢ θεολογικῆς δόγματα σαφηνίζειν ἐκ μέρους, ὧν χωρὶς οὐδεὶς ὄψεται τὸν Κύριον.
problems.why: The source does not cite Hebrews 12:14; the citation is an unwarranted addition.
problems.fix: It is right to discuss correct conduct with monks and with people in the world, and to clarify in part the teachings of natural and theological doctrine, without which no one will see the Lord.

problems.quote: holds the place of salt for the impure, but of light for the pure
problems.source_quote: ὁ ἁλὸς μὲν λόγον ἐπέχων τοῖς ἀκαθάρτοις, φωτὸς δὲ τοῖς καθαροῖς
problems.why: ἐπέχω here means 'holds back/restrains' not 'holds the place of'; salt and light are what he restrains.
problems.fix: one who holds back the word of salt for the impure, but of light for the pure
problems.ruling: Greek says 'salt holding a word' and 'light for the pure'; English adds spurious 'holds the place of' not in source.

edits.old: A practical ascetic is one who has acquired only the passionate part of the soul as free from passion.
edits.new: A practical ascetic is one who has acquired only the passive part of the soul as free from passion.

edits.old: without which no one will see the Lord (Hebrews 12:14).
edits.new: without which no one will see the Lord.

edits.old: A gnostic is one who holds the place of salt for the impure, but of light for the pure.
edits.new: A gnostic is one who holds back the word of salt for the impure, but of light for the pure.

fixed: Changed 'passionate part' to 'passive part' to match παθητικὸν μέρος.
Removed the unwarranted citation (Hebrews 12:14); the source has no such reference.
Changed 'holds the place of salt' to 'holds back the word of salt' to match ἐπέχων λόγον.

problems.quote: holds back the word of salt for the impure, but of light for the pure
problems.source_quote: ἁλὸς μὲν λόγον ἐπέχων τοῖς ἀκαθάρτοις, φωτὸς δὲ τοῖς καθαροῖς
problems.why: ἁλός = salt, but syntax misrendered: 'word of salt' should be 'salt' as substance/metaphor
problems.fix: who offers salt to the impure, but light to the pure
problems.ruling: Translates ‘ἁλὸς μὲν λόγον ἐπέχων’ as ‘holds back the word of salt’, adding ‘back’ and misreading ‘word of salt’.

problems.source_quote: ∆ίκαιον τοῖς μοναχοῖς καὶ τοῖς κοσμικοῖς περὶ πολιτείας ὀρθῆς διαλέγεσθαι
problems.why: Missing 'for monks' as subject/agent; 'It is right to discuss with monks and worldly people'
problems.fix: It is right for monks to discuss correct conduct with those in the world
problems.ruling: Greek makes discussion proper for monks and worldly people; English shifts agency to the gnostic.

edits.old: A gnostic is one who holds back the word of salt for the impure, but of light for the pure.
edits.new: A gnostic is one who offers salt to the impure, but light to the pure.

edits.old: It is right to discuss correct conduct with monks and with people in the world,
edits.new: It is right for monks and for people in the world to discuss correct conduct

fixed: The English 'holds back the word of salt' misreads ἁλὸς μὲν λόγον ἐπέχων: λόγον ἐπέχων means 'holding the place/role of', so the gnostic is salt to the impure and light to the pure. Changed to 'offers salt to the impure, but light to the pure'.

The source ∆ίκαιον τοῖς μοναχοῖς καὶ τοῖς κοσμικοῖς περὶ πολιτείας ὀρθῆς διαλέγεσθαι makes monks and worldly people the subjects of the infinitive, not the addressees. Changed to 'It is right for monks and for people in the world to discuss correct conduct'.

problems.quote: offers salt to the impure, but light to the pure
problems.source_quote: ὁ ἁλὸς μὲν λόγον ἐπέχων τοῖς ἀκαθάρτοις, φωτὸς δὲ τοῖς καθαροῖς
problems.why: ἐπέχων means 'withholds/restrains', not 'offers'; salt blinds, it is not given
problems.fix: one who withholds the word of salt from the impure, but [gives] that of light to the pure
problems.ruling: Greek says ‘salt holding a word for the impure’, not ‘offers salt’; the action is mis‑rendered.

edits.old: A gnostic is one who offers salt to the impure, but light to the pure.
edits.new: A gnostic is one who withholds the word of salt from the impure, but gives that of light to the pure.

fixed: The English 'offers salt' misstates the source: ἐπέχων means 'withholds/restrains', not 'offers'. The source says the gnostic holds the place of salt for the impure, i.e., withholds the word of salt from them, while giving light to the pure. Edited accordingly.

problems.quote: It is right for monks and for people in the world to discuss correct conduct and to clarify in part the teachings of natural and theological doctrine
problems.source_quote: ∆ίκαιον τοῖς μοναχοῖς καὶ τοῖς κοσμικοῖς περὶ πολιτείας ὀρθῆς
problems.why: The datives are the audience of διαλέγεσθαι, not the agents. It is right for the gnostic to speak to monks and laypeople, not for laypeople to teach doctrine.
problems.fix: It is right to speak to monks and people in the world about right conduct and to clarify in part such teachings of natural contemplation or theology

problems.quote: A gnostic is one who withholds the word of salt from the impure, but gives that of light to the pure.
problems.source_quote: ἁλὸς μὲν λόγον ἐπέχων τοῖς ἀκαθάρτοις
problems.why: The idiom λόγον ἐπέχων means holding the place or role of, not withholding the word, and gives is invented. The gnostic serves as salt for the impure and light for the pure.
problems.fix: A gnostic is one who serves as salt for the impure, and as light for the pure.
problems.ruling: ἐπέχων λόγον is hold the role, not withhold; parallel ἁλὸς/φωτός lacks invented 'gives.'

problems.quote: only the passive part of the soul as free from passion.
problems.source_quote: τὸ παθητικὸν μέρος τῆς ψυχῆς μόνον ἀπαθὲς
problems.why: παθητικὸν means passionate or passible (subject to passions), not passive. Calling it passive loses the technical meaning and its link to free from passion.
problems.fix: only the passionate part of the soul as free from passion.
problems.ruling: παθητικὸν is passible (passions), not inactive 'passive'; obscures link to ἀπαθὲς.

edits.old: It is right for monks and for people in the world to discuss correct conduct and to clarify in part the teachings of natural and theological doctrine
edits.new: It is right to discuss correct conduct with monks and people in the world and to clarify in part the teachings of natural and theological doctrine

edits.old: A gnostic is one who withholds the word of salt from the impure, but gives that of light to the pure.
edits.new: A gnostic is one who serves as salt for the impure, and as light for the pure.

edits.old: A practical ascetic is one who has acquired only the passive part of the soul as free from passion.
edits.new: A practical ascetic is one who has acquired only the passionate part of the soul as free from passion.

fixed: agency: fixed — datives τοῖς μοναχοῖς καὶ τοῖς κοσμικοῖς are recipients of διαλέγεσθαι, so the gnostic speaks to/with them.
mistranslation salt/light: fixed — ἁλὸς λόγον ἐπέχων means holding the role of salt, not withholding the word; removed invented gives.
mistranslation passive: fixed — τὸ παθητικὸν μέρος is the passionate part, parallel to ἀπαθὲς.

refereed.quote: withholds the word of salt from the impure, but gives that of light to the pure
refereed.source_quote: ἁλὸς μὲν λόγον ἐπέχων τοῖς ἀκαθάρτοις, φωτὸς δὲ τοῖς καθαροῖς
refereed.why: "withholds" and "gives" reverse the sense; ἐπέχω means "holds back, restrains" not "withholds from."
refereed.fix: who holds back the word of salt for the impure, but that of light for the pure
refereed.ruling: ἐπέχων = holds (gives), not withholds; reversal of sense
